name: ordinary games derive deuce advantage and completion from raw points
input: a deuce game whose lead changes twice
test:
game = Game(('A', 'B'))
for winner in 'ABABAB':
    game.record_point(winner)
assert game.displayed_score() == 'deuce'
game.record_point('A')
assert game.displayed_score() == 'advantage A'
game.record_point('B')
assert game.displayed_score() == 'deuce'
game.record_point('B')
assert game.displayed_score() == 'advantage B'
game.record_point('B')
assert game.complete and game.winner == 'B'
try:
    game.record_point('B')
    raise AssertionError('expected RuntimeError')
except RuntimeError:
    pass

name: extended tiebreaks require a two-point lead
input: a tiebreak tied at six all
test:
tiebreak = TiebreakGame(('A', 'B'))
for _ in range(6):
    tiebreak.record_point('A')
    tiebreak.record_point('B')
assert not tiebreak.complete and tiebreak.displayed_score() == '6-6'
tiebreak.record_point('A')
tiebreak.record_point('A')
assert tiebreak.complete and tiebreak.winner == 'A'
assert tiebreak.displayed_score() == '8-6'
